notes.decision: Translated 'the Twelve Zodiac-signs.' ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲥ = abbreviation/contraction of ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲟⲟⲩⲥ '12'; ⲛϩⲱⲁⲓ = singular of ⲡⲧϩⲱⲁⲓⲟⲛ 'zodiac-sign' (in glossary), here in collective plural construction. The pairing with ⲡ†ⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'the Five Stars (= planets)' confirms the standard Manichaean astronomical pair.

Rendered 'are they joined one to another.' ⲧⲏⲱ is the qualitative of ⲧⲱϩ 'be joined, be mingled.' The phrase ⲛ̄ⲉⲱ ⲛⲍⲉ functions equivalent to standard ⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'one another' — likely a Lycopolitan reduction of the reciprocal idiom (ⲉⲱ ≈ 'one' as in ⲟⲩⲁ).

Reading as 'are they from outside?' — interrogative completing the disciple's question about whether the five planets are external visitors moving through the zodiacal circle. ⲧⲟⲟ ⲛⲉ functions as an interrogative copula. Alternative reading 'from outside themselves' (with ⲧⲟⲟ as a possessive form) is also possible.

Greek δημιουργός 'craftsman, world-fashioner.' Translated 'Demiurge' as the technical Greek philosophical-theological term used in Manichaean polemics. In the apostle's answer, this Demiurge-figure is identified with 'the great Establisher / great Artisan' (ⲣⲉϩⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ / ⲧⲉⲭⲛⲓⲧⲏⲥ) = the Living Spirit who built the cosmos and bound the dark archons in the sphere.

Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ ('to set, establish, fix in order'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Translated 'establisher' to preserve the verbal-active sense: he who fixes/orders the creation. Identified here with the 'great artisan' (τεχνίτης) of line 16 — the Living Spirit as cosmic Demiurge.

Rendered 'the hour when she circles and casts them about.' Subject of ⲥⲁⲕⲱⲧⲉ and ⲥ̄ⲥⲓⲧⲉ is the feminine ⲧⲥⲫⲁⲓⲣⲁ 'sphere' (3sg.f). ⲥⲓⲧⲉ here likely the verb of casting/spinning — describing how the sphere's rotation flings the bound archons through their circuits, allowing them to operate above and below according to their fixed circuits.

notes.coptic_form: ⲉϩⲧⲣⲟ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ ⲉϩⲱⲓⲧⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ ⲉϩⲃⲓ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲧⲉ̄ ⲡⲱⲩ
notes.decision: Triple infinitive series describing the stewards' (ⲉⲡⲓⲧⲣⲟⲡⲟⲥ) and demanders' (ⲁⲓⲧⲏⲧⲏⲥ) actions: 'to compel them, to demand from them, to take what is theirs.' ϩⲧⲣⲟ from ϩⲧⲣ 'force/compel'; ϩⲱⲓⲧⲉ from ⲱⲓⲧⲉ 'demand/claim' (in glossary); ϩⲃⲓ likely Lycopolitan for ϥⲓ 'take, lift away.' The series describes the cosmic accounting/extraction system.

Greek loanwords: δίδυμος (Twins/Gemini, with Lyc. ⲁⲓⲁⲩ for ⲓⲇⲩ) and τοξότης (Archer/Sagittarius). The unusual pairing of Gemini+Sagittarius (rather than Aries+Leo+Sag in classical fire-triplicity) is governed by Manichaean cosmology, where Smoke = Mind (νοῦς) and these two signs belong to it.
Greek κριός (Ram/Aries) + Lyc. intensive ⲍⲱⲱϩ 'itself' (= ϩⲱⲱϥ) + λέων (Lion/Leo). The intensive marks Aries as the foundational fire-sign. Together = the world of Fire.

Greek loanwords: ταῦρος (Bull/Taurus), ὑδροχόος (Water-Bearer/Aquarius — Lyc. ⲍⲩⲁⲣⲏⲭⲟⲟⲥ with ⲍ for ⲩⲇ-), ζυγός (Yoke/Scales/Libra). Three signs for the world of Wind — the air-triplicity in classical astrology, here followed faithfully.

Greek καρκίνος (Crab/Cancer), παρθένος (Virgin/Virgo), ἰχθύς (Fish/Pisces). Three signs for the world of Water. The traditional water-triplicity is Cancer+Scorpio+Pisces, but here Virgo replaces Scorpio (which goes with Darkness instead), reflecting the Manichaean redistribution of zodiacal signs across the five dark worlds.

Greek αἰγόκερως 'Goat-horn' (Capricorn) and σκορπίος (Scorpion/Scorpio). The pair belongs to the world of Darkness — the deepest, fifth dark world. Note Scorpio here is removed from its classical water-triplicity and given to the lowest cosmic register.

Translated 'those whom the wicked-[ness ...]-s.' ⲛⲉⲧⲉ-ⲙⲁⲣⲉ is the negative habitual relative: 'those whom (subject) does not (verb).' The subject is ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲛⲉ 'wickedness' (cf. ⲣⲙⲃⲱⲛⲉϩ 'men of wickedness' in glossary). Final visible -ⲩ = 3pl object suffix on the lost verb. Sense: the twelve zodiac-archons are perpetually marked by/inseparable from their wickedness.

Obscure word at start of line 1, presumably a verbal predicate or carryover from page 167 (this kephalaion's opening section). Not analyzable in standard Coptic; possibly a corrupted form of a verbal predicate of the prior sentence, or an unattested Lycopolitan opener. Translated as '(...)' with the syntactic role acknowledged. The grammatical break ⲇⲉ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ('moreover, again concerning') marks the start of a new topical section — the present chapter's exposition on the five planets.

Per glossary 'way-leaders/way-showers'. In this kephalaion the term is applied technically to the five planets as the cosmic 'path-setters' that guide the courses of the heavens — the same agentive root used elsewhere for ecclesiastical guides applied here in its astrological register.

Per terminology guide, ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ = 'mind' (first of the five faculties). Here the world of smoke 'is mind' — the dark cosmological correspondence-pole of the highest light-faculty. Direct correspondential identification: the dark counterpart of the light-mind is the smoke-world, and Zeus (Jupiter) is its planet.

Per glossary: 'the Dry-One' and 'the Abomination'. Capitalized as personified cosmic entities — explicitly identified in line 9 as 'the Father and the Mother of all these'. The pair forms a dark cosmogonic dyad parallel to (and inverting) the Father/Mother of Light.

Translated 'being wreathed around them'. Although the glossary registers ⲗⲱⲭⲍ as 'defile/pollute' (Lyc reflex of ⲗⲱϫϩ̄), the present context demands a containment/encircling sense paralleling the preceding ⲕⲱⲛⲧⲟⲩ 'bind them about': Sun and Moon reign over the planets, bind them about, and circumambulate them at every hour. The verb here likely reflects ⲗⲟⲗⲍ 'wrap, twine around' rather than the defile-stem. Astrologically this names the orbital encircling of the planets by the luminaries.

ⲕⲟⲟⲍ = Lyc reflex of ⲕⲟⲟϩ 'corner' (with ⲍ for ϩ). The phrase 'three by corner' (ϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲕⲟⲟⲍ) describes the four-corner astrological division: 12 zodiacal signs distributed three to each of the four cosmic corners (the standard four trigones).

Repetition of 'Leo' is preserved in the transcription. This is most likely scribal dittography — the standard fire-trigon (Aries / Leo / Sagittarius) has only one Leo, and the parallel triads in lines 21-23 each list three distinct signs. I have rendered both occurrences faithfully without correction.

Greek ἐπίτροπος 'steward, overseer'. The cosmic governor presiding over the plundering of light from each trigon. Translated 'the steward'. Functionally similar to but not identical with the King of Honor or other named cosmic overseers.

Translated 'mounted upon him'. ⲙⲁⲍⲉ likely Lyc reflex of ⲙⲟⲩⲍ/ⲙⲟⲩⲣ in 'be set, ride upon' sense; with directional ⲁⲭⲱϥ ('upon him') the astrological sense is the planets riding through the zodiacal sign during plundering. Confidence moderate; could alternatively be 'fill upon' (ⲙⲟⲩϩ).

Read as ⲛⲧⲏⲣⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'of the dry land below' — Greek-derived ⲍⲏⲣⲁ/ⲧⲏⲣⲁ < ξηρά 'dry land', though the spelling here (ⲧϩⲧⲟⲩⲟ̄ⲣⲁ) is unusual. Eschatological-astrological sense: the affliction strikes terrestrial cattle when the fire-trigon is plundered. Spelling-uncertainty noted.

Compound ⲥⲁⲛ- ('makers/doers of') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix 'do') + ⲙⲛⲧⲃⲟⲟⲛⲉ ('evil'). Translated 'the makers of evil' — the seven (five planets + two nodes) are the cosmic agents through which the dark cosmogonic principles act. ⲥⲁⲛ- is variant of standard ⲥⲁ- (agent prefix) with epenthetic -ⲛ-.

Translated as 'ripenings' per accumulated vocabulary. The agricultural-seasonal context (paired with figs and tree-fruits, in a passage about zodiacal influence) confirms the seasonal-ripening sense over Crum's 'sickness/scab.'
Translated as 'come into being' (= ϣⲱⲡⲉ). The subject 'they' refers back to the previous page's discussion of zodiac-related cosmic phenomena.

Greek loanwords for Scorpio (Σκορπίος), Pisces (Ἰχθύς), and Cancer (Καρκίνος) — the three water signs. The text correlates these with diminishing of waters, then the air signs (Gemini/Libra/Aquarius) with diminishing of humanity, displaying classical astrological element-correspondence.
Translated as 'diminishing' — likely cognate with ⲇⲱⲭⲃⲉ 'diminish' (in glossary, Crum 511a). The substantival ⲟⲩⲃⲱⲭⲃⲉ functions as 'a diminishing/decrease.'

Translated as 'waters' (homograph of 'counsels' but here in clearly hydrological context — diminishing of waters under water-zodiac influence). Per glossary entry distinguishing the two homographs in this kephalaion.

Translated tentatively as 'year-of-failure / year of scarcity.' Etymology unclear: ⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲉ ('year') + ϣⲉⲗⲣⲉ. Possibly related to ϣⲗⲟ 'fail, be exhausted' or to ϣⲗⲱⲣ 'fresh' (Crum). The agricultural-zodiacal context of waters diminishing supports a famine/scarcity sense. Flagged as proposed term.

Greek loanwords for Gemini (Δίδυμος 'twins'), Libra (Ζυγός 'yoke'), and Aquarius (Ὑδροχόος 'water-pourer') — the three air signs. Form a paired triad with the water signs in line 3, demonstrating the elemental zodiacal scheme.

Translated as 'the imprint of humanity' — ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ in correspondential register denotes the seal/imprint by which humanity is configured cosmically. Per glossary: 'imprint/seal.' The lack and diminishing affecting humanity under air-sign influence parallels the water-diminishing under water-signs.

Greek ἀναβιβάζων 'ascending node' — astronomical term for the lunar nodes (Caput Draconis et Cauda). 'The two anabibazons' refers to the ascending and descending lunar nodes, traditionally the cosmological 'dragon's head and tail.' Retained as Greek technical term.

'The Dry one and the Moist one' — capitalized as cosmic principles. ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲩⲃⲉ corresponds to ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲇⲃⲉ in glossary ('the moist one'). The dry/moist dyad here is identified directly with Father/Mother — the primordial cosmic pair. Direct correspondential identification.

'The work takes light upon him' — referring to sun/moon. The cosmic 'work' (= the soteriological refining-economy) draws light upon the sun and moon, hence they are reckoned among the plunderers (= those who plunder light from darkness).

Translated as 'not being reckoned' — taking ⲛ̄ⲧⲁϩ as a partitive/relational ('to him/it') modulated by negative ⲉⲛ. The sense: sun and moon are not counted in the dark cosmos with stars and zodiac, since they belong to the dominion (ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲃ) of light. Reading uncertain in fine detail; structure clear.
